verdict_text: YES — the script deletes exactly the 48 buffers via a `fullmatch` on the three buffer names, casts exactly the 64 named projection matrices to bfloat16 (`.float().to(torch.bfloat16)`, equivalent to a direct cast), upcasts every remaining tensor to float32, preserves names, and asserts all four required checks (64 bfloat16, layer-0 QKV bfloat16, `embed_in` float32, 196 tensors) before writing. The 256 MiB shard limit is passed to `save_sharded_safetensors`, which is a helper module not included here; the visible logic is correct assuming that helper implements the sharding and index file as specified.
